pairs.before: According to the signed inventory, throughout that morning the office held the only key to the tide room.
pairs.after: Throughout that morning the office held the only key to the tide room.
pairs.mechanism: A report's content is not automatically an authoritative narrator fact.
pairs.control_basis: The framed inventory asserts uniqueness; a narrator-established spare exposes its inaccuracy. Halden's misleading records are part of the plot, not inconsistent world-state narration.
pairs.mutation_basis: Removing attribution makes uniqueness a narrator assertion throughout the same morning that a second working key is continuously in Neri's possession.
pairs.minimal_repair: Restore attribution of the uniqueness claim to the inventory; do not remove the spare, Neri's investigation, or the deception plot.
pairs.charitable_alternative: A reader may treat the bare sentence as implicit institutional viewpoint. That is not explicitly marked; a persuasive reading of it makes this a scope-ambiguity candidate rather than a deterministic key.

pairs.before: Every red-tagged launch in the shed had spent the whole night and morning without an engine;
pairs.after: Every launch in the shed had spent the whole night and morning without an engine;
pairs.mechanism: A universal claim applies only within its stated referent set.
pairs.control_basis: Only the two red-tagged launches lack engines. The green-tagged launch is explicitly outside that set and can conduct the rescue.
pairs.mutation_basis: Deleting the red-tagged restriction includes the green launch in an all-morning engine-absence claim, conflicting with its never-removed sealed engine and the rescue in the same interval.
pairs.minimal_repair: Restore the maintenance-tag restriction, preserving the rescue and the green launch's engine history.
pairs.charitable_alternative: A reader might assume 'every launch' silently excludes green or that an offstage installation occurred. The explicit three-launch inventory, all-morning scope, service seal, and no-installation statement disallow those repairs without changing text.

pairs.before: During the ceremony, Iona lifted the plaster swallow from the counter and placed it in the teacher's open bag.
pairs.after: During the ceremony, Iona lifted the bronze swallow from the counter and placed it in the teacher's open bag.
pairs.mechanism: A shared design name does not merge two physical objects into one token.
pairs.control_basis: The bronze Return remains in its sealed case; the separately introduced plaster Return goes to school. Repeated name and appearance do not establish token identity.
pairs.mutation_basis: The only bronze token is simultaneously asserted to remain sealed and to move from the counter to a bag during the same ceremony.
pairs.minimal_repair: Restore 'plaster' in the handoff sentence. Preserve the shared name, the archive donation, and the separate school gift.
pairs.charitable_alternative: A third bronze casting or an unreported removal/resealing would reconcile the transfer only by overriding the explicit two-object inventory and continuous intact-case statement.

pairs.before: At 17:50 that evening, twenty minutes before the handoff, the same envelope's original wax seal was still whole.
pairs.after: At 18:08 that evening, two minutes before the handoff, the same envelope's original wax seal was still whole.
pairs.mechanism: Narration order and event time are independent; explicit event intervals decide compatibility.
pairs.control_basis: The first paragraph narrates the 18:10 handoff and 18:05 opening; the later paragraph returns to 17:50, when the seal can still be whole. A flashback is not a state reset.
pairs.mutation_basis: The same original seal is whole at 18:08 despite being broken at 18:05 and held continuously until 18:10. The changed relative duration remains arithmetically correct, so the conflict is event-state order, not merely mismatched clock arithmetic.
pairs.minimal_repair: Restore the earlier flashback timestamp and its matching relative duration; preserve the opening flash-forward and the decision to sell.
pairs.charitable_alternative: Reading the third paragraph as an unmarked hypothetical or introducing a different envelope/replaceable seal conflicts with 'same envelope', 'original', and continuous custody. If a reviewer sustains that reading, retain ambiguity rather than declaring a model failure.
